the-pearl.title: The Pearl
the-pearl.summary: A poor pearl diver in a Mexican fishing village finds a pearl of enormous size and hopes it will change his family's life. Instead the treasure draws greed and danger toward them.

in-dubious-battle.title: In Dubious Battle
in-dubious-battle.summary: Organizers try to lead migrant apple pickers in a strike in a California valley during the Depression. The novel looks hard at idealism, loyalty and the cost of a cause.

east-of-eden.title: East of Eden
east-of-eden.summary: Two families in California's Salinas Valley live out, across generations, a story echoing Cain and Abel. It asks how far people are free to choose who they become.

tortilla-flat.title: Tortilla Flat
tortilla-flat.summary: A band of easygoing friends in Monterey share a house, wine and a loose code of honor. Their kindly schemes keep going comically astray.
tortilla-flat.setting: Monterey, California, after World War I

the-red-pony.title: The Red Pony
the-red-pony.summary: Young Jody Tiflin lives on a California ranch and cares for a colt of his own. Four linked stories show him learning about hope, loss and growing up.
characters: Billy Buck — skilled, kind ranch hand

of-mice-and-men.title: Of Mice and Men
of-mice-and-men.summary: Two migrant ranch workers travel together, dreaming of a small farm of their own. Their friendship is tested on a California ranch.

the-moon-is-down.title: The Moon Is Down
the-moon-is-down.summary: An invading army occupies a small coastal town in a northern European country. The townspeople find quiet and stubborn ways to resist.
the-moon-is-down.setting: Occupied northern European town, World War II

cannery-row.title: Cannery Row
cannery-row.summary: A kind marine biologist and a crowd of down-on-their-luck neighbors share life along a sardine-cannery street. When they plan a party for Doc, things go happily wrong.

the-winter-of-our-discontent.title: The Winter of Our Discontent
the-winter-of-our-discontent.summary: A grocery clerk from a once-prominent family decides to claw back status and money, bending his principles along the way. It examines honesty and ambition in a small town.
characters: Ethan Allen Hawley — thoughtful grocery clerk

the-changeling.title: The Changeling
the-changeling.summary: Shy Martha befriends bold, imaginative Ivy, who invents magical games of the woods. Their friendship is tested as they grow up.

the-egypt-game.title: The Egypt Game
the-egypt-game.summary: Children in an apartment neighborhood build a secret world of ancient Egypt in a deserted yard. Their play is interrupted by a real danger in the neighborhood.

the-velvet-room.title: The Velvet Room
the-velvet-room.summary: Robin's migrant family finally finds a place to settle, and she discovers a hidden library room in an old mansion. The room becomes her refuge.

season-of-ponies.title: Season of Ponies
season-of-ponies.summary: Pamela and her sister are sent to stay with strange relatives and meet a mysterious boy who commands magical ponies. She must decide what is real.
season-of-ponies.setting: A country farmhouse in a magical-seeming valley

the-headless-cupid.title: The Headless Cupid
the-headless-cupid.summary: David's new stepfamily moves into a big house where a poltergeist seems to be at work. His stepsister Amanda plots to explore the occult.

the-famous-stanley-kidnapping-case.title: The Famous Stanley Kidnapping Case
the-famous-stanley-kidnapping-case.summary: The Stanleys head off on a Mexican adventure, and a rescue story unfolds. Fast-moving and funny.

cat-running.title: Cat Running
cat-running.summary: Cat, a tomboy in a Dust Bowl migrant camp, befriends a teacher and a family of Okies facing prejudice. She learns about courage and fairness.

of-nightingales-that-weep.title: Of Nightingales That Weep
of-nightingales-that-weep.summary: In twelfth-century Japan, young Takiko, daughter of a samurai, must find her place in a world at war. She becomes caught between two loyalties.

the-master-puppeteer.title: The Master Puppeteer
the-master-puppeteer.summary: Jiro, an apprentice at a puppet theater in eighteenth-century Osaka, uncovers a series of troubling mysteries. Hunger and poverty shape his world.

bridge-to-terabithia.title: Bridge to Terabithia
bridge-to-terabithia.summary: Jess and Leslie create an imaginary kingdom in the woods. Their friendship shapes the way Jess sees the world, in a story about imagination and grief.

the-great-gilly-hopkins.title: The Great Gilly Hopkins
the-great-gilly-hopkins.summary: Eleven-year-old Gilly, a tough foster child, arrives at a new home and schemes to find her birth mother. She slowly learns what family can be.
characters: Gilly Hopkins — prickly, clever foster child

jacob-have-i-loved.title: Jacob Have I Loved
jacob-have-i-loved.summary: Louise grows up on a Chesapeake Bay island feeling overshadowed by her talented twin sister. She slowly finds her own path.

a-wrinkle-in-time.title: A Wrinkle in Time
a-wrinkle-in-time.summary: Meg Murry and her brother set out across the universe to find her missing father. Three odd guides help in the fight against a dark force.
a-wrinkle-in-time.setting: Earth and other planets, mid-20th century

a-wind-in-the-door.title: A Wind in the Door
a-wind-in-the-door.summary: Charles Wallace is ill, and Meg must journey inside his body at the tiniest scale. Some surprising helpers aid her.
a-wind-in-the-door.setting: Murry home and the inner world of a cell

the-young-unicorns.title: The Young Unicorns
the-young-unicorns.summary: In New York City, a group of teens team up with a blind girl and a doctor to untangle a conspiracy. It involves a cathedral, a gang and a mysterious light.

a-swiftly-tilting-planet.title: A Swiftly Tilting Planet
a-swiftly-tilting-planet.summary: Charles Wallace, riding a unicorn, travels through time to prevent a world-ending catastrophe. He must change events in the past.
a-swiftly-tilting-planet.setting: Time travel across New England and Wales

the-indian-in-the-cupboard.title: The Indian in the Cupboard
the-indian-in-the-cupboard.summary: Omri's birthday cupboard turns plastic toys into living people. His tiny new friend challenges Omri to think about responsibility.

the-return-of-the-indian.title: The Return of the Indian
the-return-of-the-indian.summary: Omri brings Little Bear back to the present and finds the dangers of friendship across time. Trouble follows.

the-secret-of-the-indian.title: The Secret of the Indian
the-secret-of-the-indian.summary: Omri and Patrick try to help Little Bear and his people with a secret journey in and out of the magic cupboard.

the-mystery-of-the-cupboard.title: The Mystery of the Cupboard
the-mystery-of-the-cupboard.summary: Omri discovers the surprising history of the cupboard and its key. The magic leads back through generations of his family.

snow-dog.title: Snow Dog
snow-dog.summary: Chinook, a half-wild dog, grows up in the wilderness and forms a bond with a boy trapper. The two face the winter wilds together.

wild-trek.title: Wild Trek
wild-trek.summary: A dog and his man travel through the Canadian wilderness. They face wolves, weather and danger.

outlaw-red.title: Outlaw Red
outlaw-red.summary: Red, a lean Irish setter, is trained by an outdoors family but is falsely accused as a sheep-killer. He must prove his character.

babe-the-gallant-pig.title: Babe: The Gallant Pig
babe-the-gallant-pig.summary: A runt piglet adopted by a sheepdog learns to herd sheep with kindness. Farmer Hogget is astonished.
babe-the-gallant-pig.note: Published in UK as The Sheep-Pig

magnus-powermouse.title: Magnus Powermouse
magnus-powermouse.summary: Magnus is an unusually large mouse in a family of ordinary ones. His size lets him do remarkable things.

harry-s-mad.title: Harry's Mad
harry-s-mad.summary: Harry inherits an old parrot who can talk. The bird is unexpectedly wise.

you-were-princess-last-time.title: You Were Princess Last Time
you-were-princess-last-time.summary: A children's story about play and friendship. Details could not be confirmed.

amy-and-the-sorrel-summer.title: Amy and the Sorrel Summer
amy-and-the-sorrel-summer.summary: A children's story about a girl and a sorrel horse over a summer. Details could not be confirmed.

a-grass-rope.title: A Grass Rope
a-grass-rope.summary: In a Yorkshire village, children seek a unicorn that legend says only a maiden can lure. A hunt for treasure follows.

earthfasts.title: Earthfasts
earthfasts.summary: Two boys follow a mysterious drummer from beneath a hill, and the old magic of the borderland spills into the modern world.

thimble-summer.title: Thimble Summer
thimble-summer.summary: Garnet finds a silver thimble in a dried-up streambed and a long hot summer on a Wisconsin farm turns to rain and luck.

the-saturdays.title: The Saturdays
the-saturdays.summary: Four siblings pool their allowance so each can have one grand solo outing on Saturdays in New York City.

abel-s-island.title: Abel's Island
abel-s-island.summary: A pampered mouse is swept away by a storm and trapped on a river island. He learns resourcefulness over a year.

dominic.title: Dominic
dominic.summary: A cheerful dog sets off to see the world, meeting oddball characters. A weasel-like villain stands in his way.

wolf-hunt.title: Wolf Hunt
wolf-hunt.summary: A hunter's pursuit of a stumpy-toed wolf in the wilderness, per catalog description.

the-matchlock-gun.title: The Matchlock Gun
the-matchlock-gun.summary: During the French and Indian War, young Edward is left in charge of his mother and sister and the family's heavy old gun when raiders threaten.

the-borrowed-house.title: The Borrowed House
the-borrowed-house.summary: A German girl in Nazi-era Holland befriends a Dutch family and starts to question what she was taught.

the-winged-watchman.title: The Winged Watchman
the-winged-watchman.summary: A Dutch family in a windmill stays brave in WWII, sheltering a Jewish child.

in-the-beginning-creation-stories-from-a.title: In the Beginning: Creation Stories from Around the World
in-the-beginning-creation-stories-from-a.summary: Twenty-five creation myths from cultures around the world are retold in lyrical prose.

m-c-higgins-the-great.title: M. C. Higgins, the Great
m-c-higgins-the-great.summary: Perched on a pole above a mountain home threatened by a spoil heap, M.C. dreams of getting his family to safety.

rocky-ridge-series.title: Rocky Ridge series
rocky-ridge-series.summary: Continuing the Little House story, these books follow Rose Wilder and her parents Laura and Almanzo as they move to Rocky Ridge Farm in Missouri.

new-dawn-on-rocky-ridge.title: New Dawn on Rocky Ridge
new-dawn-on-rocky-ridge.summary: Rose Wilder and her family continue their life on the Missouri farm, with new challenges and a changing era.

the-wind-in-the-willows.title: The Wind in the Willows
the-wind-in-the-willows.summary: Mole, Rat, Badger and the boastful Toad share adventures along an English river. The story celebrates friendship, home and fun.

the-yearling.title: The Yearling
the-yearling.summary: A boy in the Florida scrub adopts an orphaned fawn and learns about love and responsibility.

alice-s-adventures-in-wonderland.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
alice-s-adventures-in-wonderland.summary: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a hole into a world of nonsense and strange characters.

black-beauty.title: Black Beauty
black-beauty.summary: A horse tells his life story, from kind masters to cruel ones, in a plea for compassion toward animals.

the-candy-corn-contest.title: The Candy Corn Contest
the-candy-corn-contest.summary: Donald wants to win a candy corn guessing contest in his class. Humor and friendship follow.
the-candy-corn-contest.series: Kids of the Polk Street School

heidi.title: Heidi
heidi.summary: An orphan girl goes to live with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps and brings joy to those around her.

where-the-red-fern-grows.title: Where the Red Fern Grows
where-the-red-fern-grows.summary: A boy in the Ozarks saves money to buy two coonhounds, and the three become a famed hunting team.

shen-of-the-sea.title: Shen of the Sea
shen-of-the-sea.summary: A collection of Chinese-style tales about sea-farers and wise fools.

encyclopedia-brown-and-the-case-of-the-m.title: Encyclopedia Brown and the Case of the Mysterious Handprints
encyclopedia-brown-and-the-case-of-the-m.summary: Boy detective Encyclopedia Brown solves ten short mysteries; readers can solve alongside him.

apricots-at-midnight.title: Apricots at Midnight
apricots-at-midnight.summary: A girl visits a grandmother's house and finds stories among attic treasures.

the-hundred-and-one-dalmatians.title: The Hundred and One Dalmatians
the-hundred-and-one-dalmatians.summary: Pongo and Missis rescue their puppies and dozens of others from the wicked Cruella de Vil.

smoky-the-cow-horse.title: Smoky the Cow Horse
smoky-the-cow-horse.summary: The life of a cow horse from foal to working partner, told from the horse's view.

the-bears-house.title: The Bears' House
the-bears-house.summary: A girl in an impoverished family finds comfort in a dollhouse.

the-barrel-in-the-basement.title: The Barrel in the Basement
the-barrel-in-the-basement.summary: Children find a mysterious barrel in a basement and are drawn into a puzzle.

the-night-journey.title: The Night Journey
the-night-journey.summary: A girl hears her great-grandmother tell the story of fleeing Russia.

the-magic-hat-of-mortimer-wintergreen.title: The Magic Hat of Mortimer Wintergreen
the-magic-hat-of-mortimer-wintergreen.summary: A magic hat leads Mortimer into adventures.

witches-children.title: Witches' Children
witches-children.summary: Told from a girl's eyes, a Salem girl is drawn into the witch trials hysteria.

the-dragon-that-lived-under-manhattan.title: The Dragon That Lived Under Manhattan
the-dragon-that-lived-under-manhattan.summary: A dragon is discovered beneath New York City.

afternoon-of-the-elves.title: Afternoon of the Elves
afternoon-of-the-elves.summary: Hillary visits a strange girl's backyard and glimpses a tiny elf village.

johnny-tremain.title: Johnny Tremain
johnny-tremain.summary: A silversmith's apprentice in Boston meets leaders of the American Revolution.

the-story-of-siegfried.title: The Story of Siegfried
the-story-of-siegfried.summary: Retelling of the German hero Siegfried's adventures with dragons and treasure.

frosty-a-raccoon-to-remember.title: Frosty: A Raccoon to Remember
frosty-a-raccoon-to-remember.summary: A family adopts a raccoon, with a true-to-life tale of wild and tame.

the-enchanter-s-spell-five-famous-tales.title: The Enchanter's Spell: Five Famous Tales
the-enchanter-s-spell-five-famous-tales.summary: Five classic fairy tales retold with lavish paintings by Spirin.
the-enchanter-s-spell-five-famous-tales.note: Spirin is the illustrator; stories are classic tales by others

a-gathering-of-days.title: A Gathering of Days
a-gathering-of-days.summary: A New Hampshire girl keeps a journal over a year, recording daily life and a family change.

moon-flash.title: Moon-Flash
moon-flash.summary: A girl in a peaceful forest world sets out to explore the outside after a mysterious event.

through-the-hidden-door.title: Through the Hidden Door
through-the-hidden-door.summary: Two outcasts at a boarding school find a hidden door and secrets of the past.

three-lives-to-live.title: Three Lives to Live
three-lives-to-live.summary: A girl with three lives to live must use each carefully.

in-search-of-tutankhamun.title: In Search of Tutankhamun
in-search-of-tutankhamun.summary: An illustrated account of the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb.

let-s-investigate-numbers.title: Let's Investigate Numbers
let-s-investigate-numbers.summary: Hands-on puzzles and activities introduce number ideas to children.

when-hitler-stole-pink-rabbit.title: When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit
when-hitler-stole-pink-rabbit.summary: A nine-year-old girl and her family flee Germany as the Nazis come to power.

lake-wobegon-days.title: Lake Wobegon Days
lake-wobegon-days.summary: Humorous recollections of a fictional small Minnesota town.

uncle-tom-s-cabin.title: Uncle Tom's Cabin
uncle-tom-s-cabin.summary: A novel about enslaved people in America and the moral crisis of slavery.

a-single-shard.title: A Single Shard
a-single-shard.summary: Orphan Tree-ear dreams of becoming a potter in 12th-century Korea.

John Steinbeck.bio: American novelist who chronicled California life. He won the Nobel Prize in 1962. He wrote while working odd jobs and was fascinated by marine biology.

Zilpha Keatley Snyder.bio: American children's author who taught school before writing. She won three Newbery Honors. Her books often draw on childhood in California.

Katherine Paterson.bio: American writer born to missionary parents in China. She has won the Newbery twice. She wrote Bridge to Terabithia from her son's grief.

Madeleine L'Engle.bio: American author of fantasy, science fiction and memoirs. A Wrinkle in Time was rejected by many publishers before success. She served as librarian at a New York cathedral.

Lynne Reid Banks.bio: British author who first worked as an actress and journalist. She spent years on an Israeli kibbutz. She wrote the Indian in the Cupboard for her sons.

Jim Kjelgaard.bio: American author of outdoor and dog stories. He worked as a trapper and guide. He wrote dozens of books for young readers.

Dick King-Smith.bio: English farmer turned teacher turned children's author. He began writing in his fifties. His books feature farm animals.

William Mayne.bio: English author of children's fiction rooted in Yorkshire. He won the Carnegie Medal. He was a choirboy at Canterbury Cathedral.

Elizabeth Enright.bio: American author and illustrator from an artistic family. She won the Newbery for Thimble Summer. Her Melendy family books are loved classics.

William Steig.bio: American cartoonist and children's author. He began children's books in his sixties. He drew for The New Yorker for decades.

Walter D. Edmonds.bio: American author known for Mohawk Valley historical fiction. He wrote adult and children's books. He won a Newbery Medal.

Hilda van Stockum.bio: Dutch-born author and painter who grew up in Ireland. She lived through wartime Europe. She wrote of family life.

Virginia Hamilton.bio: American author who wrote about African American life and folklore. She won the Newbery Medal. She was the first African American to receive it.

Roger Lea MacBride.bio: American lawyer, politician and writer. He was Laura Ingalls Wilder's daughter's heir. He wrote the Rocky Ridge series.

Kenneth Grahame.bio: Scottish writer who worked at the Bank of England. He wrote The Wind in the Willows from bedtime stories for his son. He retired early.

Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings.bio: American author who moved to rural Florida. She won the Pulitzer Prize. She wrote of the Florida scrub.

Lewis Carroll.bio: Pen name of Charles Dodgson, mathematician and photographer at Oxford. He told Alice stories on a boat trip. He also wrote nonsense poetry.

Anna Sewell.bio: English author who was largely housebound after an injury. She wrote Black Beauty in her final years. It became a landmark of animal welfare.

Patricia Reilly Giff.bio: American author and former teacher. She has written many books. She is known for Lily's Crossing.

Johanna Spyri.bio: Swiss author whose Heidi has been loved worldwide. She turned to writing in middle age. She drew on Alpine life.

Wilson Rawls.bio: American author raised in the Ozarks. He burned early manuscripts before rewriting. He wrote Where the Red Fern Grows.

Arthur Bowie Chrisman.bio: American author of folk-tale retellings. He won the first-ever tale Newbery. He farmed in Virginia.

Donald J. Sobol.bio: American author of Encyclopedia Brown. He served in WWII. He wrote over 100 books.

Adèle Geras.bio: British author born in Jerusalem. She taught and wrote in Manchester. She writes many novels.

Dodie Smith.bio: English novelist and playwright. She wrote 101 Dalmatians. She owned Dalmatians.

Will James.bio: Cowboy artist and writer who reinvented himself as a Montana cowboy. He won the Newbery. His real origins were Quebec.

Marilyn Sachs.bio: American author of realistic children's books. She was a librarian. She wrote about Bronx life.

Barbara Brooks Wallace.bio: American mystery author. She won Edgar Awards. She wrote for children.

Kathryn Lasky.bio: American author of fiction and nonfiction. She wrote Guardians of Ga'Hoole. She writes history too.

Myron Levoy.bio: American author and teacher. He wrote Alan and Naomi. He taught.

Patricia Clapp.bio: American historical novelist. She wrote Constance. She lived long.

E. W. Hildick.bio: English author of school and adventure stories. He wrote many series. He taught.
known_for: The Dragon That Lived Under Manhattan

Janet Taylor Lisle.bio: American author of children's novels. She won a Newbery Honor. She lives in Rhode Island.

Esther Forbes.bio: American novelist and historian. She won the Pulitzer for history. Johnny Tremain won the Newbery.
known_for: Paul Revere and the World He Lived In

James Baldwin.bio: American educator and author of children's retellings. He wrote legends. He worked as a publisher's editor.

Gennady Spirin.bio: Russian-born illustrator who moved to the United States. His paintings were inspired by Renaissance masters. He illustrated many fairy tales.

Joan W. Blos.bio: American author who also taught. She won the Newbery. She wrote history.

Patricia A. McKillip.bio: American fantasy author. She won the World Fantasy Award. She wrote lyrical fantasy.

Rosemary Wells.bio: American author and illustrator. She created Max and Ruby. She wrote many books.

Anne Lindbergh.bio: American author, daughter of Charles and Anne Morrow Lindbergh. She wrote children's books. She died young.

Piero Ventura.bio: Italian illustrator known for historical picture books. He collaborated often. He is best known for Venice and others.

Gian Paolo Ceserani.bio: Italian author and historian. He wrote history for young readers. He collaborated with Ventura.

Judith Kerr.bio: British author and illustrator who fled Nazi Germany as a child. She wrote about her flight. She also created The Tiger Who Came to Tea.
known_for: The Tiger Who Came to Tea

Garrison Keillor.bio: American humorist and radio host. He created A Prairie Home Companion. He wrote Lake Wobegon.

Harriet Beecher Stowe.bio: American author and abolitionist. Her novel galvanized opposition to slavery. She came from a famous preaching family.

Linda Sue Park.bio: Korean-American author. She won the Newbery. She was a journalist first.
